To K's mind L would not even shirk from letting down his own political friends who had fought the Nazis side by side with him, if only he expected some benefit for himself from such treachery. K quoted two examples of this in great detail. The gist of his story was that when L and K were both interned, L on being questioned about K's political loyalty had held back with information he could have given in respect of K's underground work against the Nazis in Germany. L had not gone as far as to denounce K as a Nazi-sympathiser, but - as K had found out by a very unexpected chance - he had given somewhat evasive answers, indicating in a rather subtle way that he was not really quite sure of K's reliability. His motive was in the opinion of K that he expected to clear himself from suspicion by dissociating himself from the "suspect" K. L's action was the more so despicable as for years he had been in the closest possible collaboration with K in a very tough and most dangerous struggle with the Nazis. Therefore he would have been one of the few persons who could have given truthfully the strongest evidence in K's favour. Further, it was known to him that during the period in question, namely at the beginning of their internment they were both in a very serious position.

K's picture of L's character is a very condemning one and the question arises whether his judgment has been biased by his anger about the incident mentioned above and by his business-differences with L. I believe that K's verdict is sound and arrived at after he had given the most careful consideration to all sides of the matter. In his conversation with me he analysed L's character in a far more detailed way than I could describe even in this lengthy report. He never lost sight of points which might be held in L's favour as for instance his genuine hatred of the Nazis (though this does not mean that L is genuinely pro-British). On my specific question K said that he thought it unlikely that there were any "dark points" in L's. He did not think that L was hiding from the authorities any important events of or connected with his past.

My short and only interview with L and - perhaps more so - the tricky way he instructs his own solicitor rather confirm the correctness of K's views on L and they have certainly brought nothing to light which would indicate that K was wrong. My personal impression is that L is a nasty bit of work and I would not trust him a yard.

Re your enquiry about the Nazi law of Expatriation I have been promised the full text of it by to-morrow and I will write you again after perusal.

With best regards I am yours sincerely,
